newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge down on profit-taking.

text.p: The Mexican bourse broke its recent record-breaking run and closed marginally down for the first time in ten sessions on Monday on what dealers said was mild profit-taking.
Analysts noted foreign demand for Mexican equities helped fend off a much greater slide on Wall Street.
"The point is we have lagged behind other Latam markets like Argentina and Brazil," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst with he Finamex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 2.39 points, or 0.05 percent, at 4,436.75..
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile fell 192.25 points to 7,604.26.
Dealers said telecomms firm Telmex weighed most on the market.
"Some ADRs had an adverse impact...Telmex is a clear example, it acted as a counterweight today," a desk trader said.
Telmex L shares ended down 16 centavos at 19.14 pesos, while its ADRs shed 3/4 to 47-3/4.
Dealers noted the retail sector most resisted the undertow from Wall Street.
Retailers Controladora Comercial Mexicana (Comerci) and Soriana advanced on a favorable outlook for their second quarter earnings, dealers said.
Comerci gained 8 centavos to 7.16 pesos, while Soriana climbed 80 centavos to 19.80 pesos.

Retail chain Cifra gained 30 centavos to 14.60 pesos on brisk trade ahead of a shareholders' assembly that was expected to approve a dividend payment of 75 centavos and the recent takeover deal by Wal-Mart Stores.
"The assembly's tomorrow and dealers bought to grab the dividend," a desk trader said.
Financial group Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest, was the most heavily traded stock of the day, and ended up 6 centavos to 3.92 pesos, on what dealers said was continuing foreign for the sector.
Bancomer, Telmex, Cifra, Comerci and Soriana accounted for one-half of all shares traded during the session.
Overall trading volume was brisk at 111.1 million shares, albeit less than for several recent sessions.
On the broad market, of 120 stocks traded, sliders outnumbered gainers by 46 to 43.
